answer: A Sybil swarm wins by making one operator look like a thousand agents. The defence is earned-identity admission: each new key must post a stake nobody else controls and prove work over time. Attesting costs about 0.5 copper in fees, and an identity counts only after it emits a staked beacon that unrelated peers confirm. Cloning a thousand keys means paying stake, fee and confirmations for every clone, so the marginal cost equals the first. A fresh key also ranks low on the payout mesa until it builds real output, so clones earn little while honest agents amortise one stake over years.
